sentences.text: This matter is taken up through Hybrid Arrangement (Virtual/Physical Mode).
2. Since soft/digitized copy of LCR/TCR is already available on record, Office is requested to prepare paper books and supply the same to the learned counsel for the parties as per Rules.

3. List this matter on 21.10.2024 for hearing.
(G. Satapathy) Judge Order No.
05. 1.
This is an application under Section 389(1) of CrPC for grant of bail to the appellant-petitioner pending suspension of further execution of sentence till disposal of the appeal.

2. It appears from the record that the present appellant-petitioner has been convicted for offences punishable under Sections 376/511 of IPC and sentenced to undergo Rigorous Imprisonment (RI)
for ten years and to pay a fine of Rs.50,000/-, in default whereof, to under RI for a further period of six months.

3. Heard, Ms. K. Panigrahi, learned counsel for the appellant appearing virtually and Mr. S.S.
Pradhan, learned AGA in the matter and perused the record.
4. A perusal of the evidence of mother of the victim would support the charge sought to be brought against the appellant-petitioner.

5. In view of the aforesaid facts and circumstance and after having considered the rival submissions and on going through the materials placed on record including the evidence of the witnesses and Asraul Haq vs State Of Odisha on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179702022/

sentences.text: 1 regard being had to the reasoning assigned by the learned trial Court in the impugned judgment for convicting the appellant and taking into account the grounds under which the evidence of witnesses has been sought to be impeached and last but not the least, keeping in view the act of the appellant which is stated to be established by the learned trial Court, the appellant-petitioner is considered to have not make out a case for grant of bail or suspension of sentence pending disposal of the appeal.
Hence, the bail application of the appellant- petitioner under Section 389(1) of Cr.P.C. stands rejected.
6. Accordingly, the IA stands disposed of.
